messages.content: Propose an ordered list of hypotheses from the registered IDs only. Choose model structures only; do not estimate numeric parameters. Return an object matching this JSON schema exactly: {"items":[{"hypothesis_id":"SENSOR_BIAS","rationale":"…","evidence_refs":["obs:0:1.200"]}]}. Each item requires hypothesis_id, rationale, and evidence_refs; no additional properties are allowed. Allowed IDs: SENSOR_BIAS, VELOCITY_OFFSET, SPEED_STEP, ACTUATOR_DELAY, AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET), AND(SENSOR_BIAS,SPEED_STEP), AND(SENSOR_BIAS,ACTUATOR_DELAY), AND(VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP), AND(VELOCITY_OFFSET,ACTUATOR_DELAY), AND(SPEED_STEP,ACTUATOR_DELAY), AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP), AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET,ACTUATOR_DELAY), AND(SENSOR_BIAS,SPEED_STEP,ACTUATOR_DELAY), AND(VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP,ACTUATOR_DELAY), SENSOR_STUCK, SENSOR_SPIKE_OR_UNRELIABLE, OBJECT_MISSING_OR_DROPPED, BELT_STOP_OR_MOTION_LOSS, POST_VERIFICATION_CHANGE, UNKNOWN_OR_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE

message.content: {"items": [{"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "The triple combination achieves the lowest RMSE (0.007901) among all passing structures, indicating the best fit to the observed target trajectory without overfitting beyond the supported model space.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "This pair yields a very low RMSE (0.010353), suggesting that velocity offset and speed step together explain most of the systematic deviation observed in the target's x-position.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "Combining sensor bias with a speed step produces an RMSE (0.011154) comparable to the velocity-offset-plus-speed-step model, supporting a mixed sensor and motion explanation.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "SPEED_STEP", "rationale": "As a single-factor model, SPEED_STEP achieves the lowest RMSE (0.011155), indicating that a change in belt speed is a strong primary explanation for the observed position drift.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET)", "rationale": "This pair fits well (RMSE 0.014477) and is consistent with a constant sensor bias compounded by a steady velocity offset, though it is outperformed by models including a speed step.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "VELOCITY_OFFSET", "rationale": "A constant velocity offset alone fits the data reasonably (RMSE 0.014812), suggesting the belt may be moving slightly faster or slower than commanded.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "SENSOR_BIAS", "rationale": "A constant sensor bias explains a portion of the observation error (RMSE 0.014551), but the residual pattern suggests additional dynamic factors are present.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}]}
